criteria.criterion: A gh test in crates/athena-core/src/gh/tests.rs: check runs with the required CI_AGGREGATE_JOB completed green plus another check run in_progress classify as Checks::Pending, and a land_pr run against the fake host makes no merge call (merge_requested false). Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh::`.
criteria.evidence: These tests passed: an_unfinished_optional_run_makes_the_checks_pending_and_even_a_red_required_run_stays_red, which asserts Pending for queued, in_progress and waiting next to a green required run, and a_pull_request_with_the_required_check_green_and_another_in_progress_is_pending_and_not_merged. The second sends land_pr through Rig::run with merge_via_rest on, and FakeHost.check_report calls the production classify_checks. It asserts merges == 0, merge_requested false, checks Some(Pending) and the link Open. Without the new `unfinished` rule the optional run would read Green and the merge would be called, so the test fails without the fix. Result: 103 passed, 0 failed.

criteria.criterion: A classify test shows a failed optional check run (completed, failure) with the required check green is still Green with a note, and a failed required check is Red. Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh::`.
criteria.evidence: The same new classify test asserts that [required success, head_run failure] is Green with exactly one note. It also asserts that [required failure, head_run success] and [required failure, optional in_progress] are both Red. The existing only_the_required_check_decides_and_optional_failures_become_notes also passes.

criteria.criterion: A gh test: when the fake host's merge returns an error containing 'Repository rule violations' while checks are not all complete, land_pr returns a pending/waiting result rather than Err. Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh::`.
criteria.evidence: a_merge_refused_for_rule_violations_while_checks_are_pending_is_a_wait passed. It uses the script [Green, Pending] and merge_error 'Repository rule violations found', and gets Ok with merges == 1, checks Pending, link Open, merge_requested true, a warning naming the refusal, and the stored link equal to the report's. Three negative tests also passed: a_merge_refused_for_rule_violations_with_the_checks_settled_stays_an_error (still Err when checks are green) and another_merge_refusal_while_checks_are_pending_stays_an_error (a different refusal text is still Err).

criteria.criterion: A drain test in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs: a merge refused for rule violations is reported as waiting to merge (not a failed landing), the run does not stop, and the next job is worked. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli drain`.
criteria.evidence: Two tests passed. a_job_waiting_to_merge_is_not_a_failure_and_the_run_goes_on_to_the_next_job runs drain_concurrent and asserts stop == QueueEmpty, no failed_item, 'land a' called once, b landed (landed == 1), and a's landing text starts with 'waiting to merge'. a_merge_refused_for_rule_violations_while_checks_are_pending_is_reported_as_waiting asserts that landing_from_report turns an Open report with checks Pending and merge_requested true into Landing::Waiting; Red, Green, None and Err stay NotLanded, and Landed stays Landed. In production, LandStep::Waiting returns ItemEnd::Waiting before `failures += 1`, then pass_over, so nothing is retried and no failure is counted. Result: 41 unit tests passed, plus 18 drain integration tests.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has a new entry describing waiting on pending check runs and treating a rule-violation merge refusal as waiting.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. There is a new bullet under [Unreleased] ### Fixed. criteria.criterion: Doc comments on classify_checks and wait_for_checks are updated to state that any queued or in-progress check run makes the verdict pending.
criteria.evidence: Read in the diff. The classify_checks doc (client.rs) now says 'Any check run on the commit that is still queued or in progress (any status but completed), the required one or an optional one, makes the verdict Checks::Pending'. Step 1 of the wait_for_checks doc (early.rs) now says 'Any check run on the head that is still queued or in progress, required or not, keeps the verdict pending'. findings.summary: A rule-violation refusal is recognised by matching the error text.
findings.evidence: is_rule_violation does format!("{refusal:#}").contains("Repository rule violations"). The accepted reading chose this. The risk is reduced because land_pr reads the checks again and treats the refusal as a wait only if they are Pending; with settled checks it stays an error. A structured status or error code from the host's merge reply would be sturdier if the client exposes one.

findings.summary: A check run that never finishes now holds the merge forever.
findings.evidence: classify_checks treats every status other than 'completed' as unfinished (queued, in_progress, waiting, requested, pending). A run that stays queued, for example one waiting for a manual approval, keeps the job reported as 'waiting to merge' on every run without saying which run is holding it. This is what the request asks for, but naming the unfinished run in the report would help the operator.

findings.summary: The land_pr rule-violation test fakes the second check read with a scripted verdict instead of check-run JSON.
findings.evidence: a_merge_refused_for_rule_violations_while_checks_are_pending_is_a_wait sets host.script = [Green, Pending] rather than using the new runs field. It still exercises the production re-read and wait branch.

summary: The change does what was asked, and I recommend accepting it. The root cause is fixed: classify_checks now reports Pending while any check run on the pull request head is unfinished. A failed required check is still Red, and a failed optional check is still only a note. So land_pr does not ask for a merge while a check such as the history check is still running. As a second guard, a merge refused with 'Repository rule violations' while checks are still pending (confirmed by reading the checks again) now gives a waiting report instead of an error. The drain shows that job as 'waiting to merge', does not retry it or count it as a failure, and goes on to the next job. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core gh::` (103 passed) and `cargo test -p athena-cli drain` (41 unit and 18 integration tests passed); the new tests cover every behaviour criterion and would fail without the fix. `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean when I ran it, and Athena's recorded clippy and test runs passed. The CHANGELOG entry and the doc comments are updated, and only files on the expected-deliverables list changed. Three small notes, none blocking: a rule-violation refusal is recognised by matching the error text (the accepted reading chose this, and the second check read limits the risk); a check run that never finishes holds the merge forever without naming that run; and one land_pr test fakes the second check read with a scripted verdict instead of check-run JSON.
